$comment: Function manifest for an agent loop. Each entry is one tool: `command` is a PowerShell template (apply Invoke-AgentStep.ps1 to it so the caller gets {ok, exitCode, stdout, stderr} back). `cost` and `needsApp` exist so the agent can budget: the app-free steps are seconds, the app steps are minutes. Paths are relative to the repo root. See docs/AGENT-RUNBOOK.md.
name: videopad-pipeline

tools.name: videopad_gate
tools.description: Regression gate. Rebuilds every example spec and asserts byte-identical output. Needs no VideoPad. Run this before and after touching the writer, and after any spec edit; if it fails, the writer or a committed example changed and nothing downstream is trustworthy.

specs.description: Optional subset of spec files to check, e.g. ["cut5-cadence.json"]. Omit to check all.

specArgs.description: Derived, not model-supplied: built from specs as ' -Spec a.json,b.json'.

tools.returns: JSON array of {Spec, Output, Result}; Result is 'identical' or 'changed'.
tools.okMeans: Every spec reproduced its .vpj byte for byte.

tools.name: videopad_build
tools.description: Compile a JSON edit spec into a .vpj project. Deterministic and app-free. Rejects bad specs with exit 1 and a one-line reason on stderr: unknown effect name, out beyond the media at that speed, speed <= 0, overlapping or oversize fades, missing source, output file locked.

spec.description: Path to the spec JSON, e.g. "examples/cut5-cadence.json". Relative paths inside the spec resolve against the spec's own folder.

tools.returns: {Output, DurationMs, Segments[]} where each segment reports StartMs/EndMs/LengthMs/Speed/InMs/OutMs/FadeInMs/FadeOutMs/Flip/AudioGainDb/AudioFadeInMs/AudioFadeOutMs/OffsetMs/Mute/Effects/AudioEffects/VideoHandle/AudioHandle/ReusedPair. AudioEffectCount is reported alongside EffectCount.
tools.okMeans: The .vpj was written; DurationMs is what the app will show.

tools.name: videopad_diff
tools.description: Field-level diff of two .vpj files, records matched by handle, dataN blobs decoded before comparing. Use it to prove a round-trip was clean, or to see exactly what the app rewrote. Expect thumb/thumbpos to differ on a round-trip: the app zeroes its thumbnail cache.

a.description: Left file, normally what the writer produced.

b.description: Right file, normally the autosave capture.

tools.returns: Text lines '  <record> <field> 'old' -> 'new'' and a count, or 'no differences'.
tools.okMeans: Exit 0 even when there are differences: this is a report, not a check. The caller decides what differences are acceptable.

tools.name: videopad_load
tools.description: Open a .vpj in VideoPad unattended, answering the expected 'Damaged File / Try Load' checksum prompt automatically. Closes any running instance first (VideoPad is single-instance and silently drops the file argument otherwise). Never force-kills.

project.description: Full or repo-relative path to the .vpj.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the project title to appear.

tools.returns: {Loaded, Title, PromptDismissed, PromptCount, Modals, ElapsedSeconds, Message}.
tools.okMeans: Loaded=true, i.e. a title matching the project appeared and no prompt is still waiting.

tools.name: videopad_roundtrip
tools.description: Load a project, wait for VideoPad to rewrite its autosave file, then diff the capture. The capture is the app's own serialisation of what its parser absorbed - the cheapest proof that a written field was understood. Takes one autosave period (~100 s), so it is the slow way to answer a question the gate cannot.

logPath.description: Log to write, e.g. "out/oracle/cut6.log". The capture lands beside it as <name>.roundtrip.vpj.

capture.description: Derived from logPath by replacing the extension with '.roundtrip.vpj'.

tools.returns: The diff text (see videopad_diff) plus a log whose RESULT line says CAPTURED or TIMEOUT.
tools.okMeans: CAPTURED and a diff showing only thumbnail fields, or only changes you can explain.

tools.name: videopad_export
tools.description: Render the open sequence to a video file, unattended, and check the duration. The export dialog is driven by real window messages; the output file is discovered rather than named, then moved to outputPath. Budget roughly twice the sequence duration plus half a minute.

outputPath.description: Where the finished .mp4 goes; parent folder is created.

project.description: Optional .vpj to open first. Omit to export whatever is already open.

expectedDurationMs.description: Expected duration in ms; the tool warns past one 24 fps frame. Take it from videopad_build's DurationMs.

tools.returns: {OutputPath, SizeBytes, DurationSeconds, DurationMs, ExpectedDurationMs, DurationDeltaMs, SourceFile, Verified, Message}.
tools.okMeans: A readable file exists at outputPath with the expected duration, so Verified=true.

tools.name: videopad_step
tools.description: Escape hatch: run any other command (an out/oracle verify script, ffmpeg, git) and get the same JSON envelope back. Use it for the frame-MAE checks in out/oracle/, which are the only way to prove that a *rendered* frame says what the spec intended.

command.description: A PowerShell command line, run from the repo root.

tools.returns: Whatever the step prints, plus {ok, exitCode, seconds, stdout, stderr} from the runner.

loop: videopad_roundtrip (only when a field's meaning is in doubt)
videopad_step (frame MAE, only when the claim is about pixels)
invariants: The gate is the only oracle that needs no app; never spend an app step on a question it can answer.
A .vpj is never hand-edited: unknown fields are preserved only when the writer does the edit.
The checksum is never repaired; 'Damaged File / Try Load' is the expected path.
VideoPad is closed with WM_CLOSE, never killed.
No verification claim without naming the oracle: gate, round-trip diff, or frame MAE.
